newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman set to launch first GSM mobile network.
newsitem.headline: Oman set to launch first GSM mobile network.

text.p: Oman's General Telecommunications Organisation (GTO) said on Thursday it would launch the Gulf country's first GSM mobile telephone network at midnight local time (2000 gmt).

In its first phase, the Global System for Mobile Telecommunications (GSM) service would have a capacity of 30,000 lines, rising to 100,000 lines when the network is completed in 1997, a GTO official told Reuters.
The German electronics company Siemens AG won a 33 million mark ($22 million) order for the turnkey mobile network in May.
The GTO official said the first phase would cover the capital Muscat, Zufar province in the west, Batinah in the south, Sur in the southeast and Musandam in the north.
After its completion, the network would cover the entire country, the official added.
The GTO encouraged the public to continue using the current mobile telephone system -- which already covered the entire country -- in addition to the new GSM network, he said.
Some 9,000 mobile telephones are already in use in Oman, according to official statistics.
"We have reduced the monthly rent of the old system from 20 Omani rials ($53) to three rials, compared with six rials for the new system," the official said.

Still, Omanis were rushing to rent the new mobile phones, he said. "The desire to obtain the GSM by the Omani public is huge by any standards," he said. No figure for subscribers was immediately available.
Several companies were competing for a share of the GSM market, with the new mobile telephones selling at 70 outlets for between 145 and 295 rials, the official said. ($1 = 0.38
